segments.title: Chương 272: 0274【Chọc sếp lớn vui vẻ】
segments.content:
Tao Xue reluctantly left the little stall.

Chen Guiliang chuckled, "What, still hoping to find a hidden gem?"

"In novels and TV shows, the main character always finds treasures when browsing antique stalls," Tao Xue said, full of fantasies about it.

Bian Guanyue said, "If there were any treasures, they would have been found long ago."

"That's not necessarily true," Tao Xue said.

Bian Guanyue asked, "Do you know anything about antiques?"

Of course, Tao Xue didn't. She tried to save face, "But I like literature. I've read a lot of classic novels. I can definitely tell if those old books are real or fake."

Bian Guanyue smiled.

To prove her point, Tao Xue ran over to a stall that sold a lot of books, picked up several, and began flipping through them pretentiously.

In Beijing, people who sell antique books can generally be divided into four types.

The first type are the true experts. These people usually run their own shops and won't be found at a stall. Plus, they ask for high prices.

The second type are professional scammers. They play dumb in all sorts of ways, disguising themselves as ignorant fools, saying things like the item was passed down from their ancestors and that they usually use the book to prop up a table leg.

The third type are second or third-hand dealers. Although they also don't know how to appraise antique books, they understand the market value very well. They have their own supply channels and know which books sell well and which can fetch a high price.

The fourth type are the old hands of the trade. They lack systematic knowledge but have extremely rich experience. They can rattle off all sorts of jargon and trade terms, but they're at a loss when they encounter something beyond their experience.

The stall owner before them belonged to the third type. The antique books on his stall were all mass-produced by villagers from a certain village. He could get as many as you wanted!

"Miss, you've got a good eye. The one in your hand is no street-stall item. It's a genuine official Suzhou-Hangzhou woodblock edition from the Qianlong era!"

The stall owner, about 50 years old, lowered his voice conspiratorially, "You know Beijing is hosting the Olympics, right? A lot of places are being demolished. This book was dug out from an old warehouse by a demolition crew last year. Take a look at this silk cover. See it? Gold thread! If you shine one of those banknote-checking pens on it, you can see the anti-counterfeit watermark clear as day!"

Chen Guiliang laughed, "Ancient books had gold thread watermarks? Why didn't they use that technology to make banknotes back then?"

The stall owner said with great authority, "They were called bank drafts back then. The bank drafts in TV shows aren't reliable; the directors are uncultured. Real Qing Dynasty bank drafts had this kind of gold thread watermark."

Tao Xue was a bit confused and turned to ask Chen Guiliang, "Did Qing Dynasty bank drafts really have gold thread watermarks?"

"Pfft!" Bian Guanyue couldn't help but burst out laughing.

If you had wandered through Beijing's antique market a few years ago, you might have actually been able to find a hidden gem among the thread-bound books. That was because the focus of stall owners and customers generally wasn't on antique books.

But at the 2002 Jiade Autumn Auction, the "Collected Letters of Ming Dynasty Notables from the Qian Jing tang Collection" sold for the sky-high price of 9.9 million yuan. Antique stall owners across the country suddenly started paying attention to ancient books, and professional book-forging teams gradually emerged.

Chen Guiliang reminded her, "The more exquisite the binding and paper, the more you should avoid it. If a fine piece like that were real, the owner would have taken it to an auction house long ago."

The stall owner glanced at Chen Guiliang. "Young man, you know your stuff." He pointed to a few books next to them. "These I really did find myself. They're all genuine. They're definitely not worth millions, but a few hundred yuan is the market price."

Tao Xue picked up those tattered thread-bound books to look at them.

Chen Guiliang glanced at two of them and saw that they were all early Republican era woodblock prints, mass-produced modern thread-bound books. And their condition was extremely poor.

They were genuine, alright, but at most they were worth a few yuan.

As Tao Xue was flipping through them, Chen Guiliang caught sight of one that was handwritten.

He took it and saw that half of the book had been soaked in water. Many of the characters were indistinct.

But the title on the cover was still legible: "A Record of Things Seen and Heard on River Defense."

Flipping it open and reading carefully, he discovered the author was a Tongzhi in charge of river affairs in the Qing Dynasty, and the book's contents were all his technical summaries from working on water conservancy projects.

It wasn't much of a hidden gem, but this book was indeed a little interesting.

"Boss, how much for this book?" Chen Guiliang asked.

The stall owner glanced at it. "This one's 1800."

Chen Guiliang said, "Didn't you just say a few hundred yuan?"

The stall owner explained, "Those Republican ones are a few hundred. This one is from the Qing Dynasty. I can read traditional characters, and it even says 'thirty-ninth year of the Qianlong reign' inside."

Chen Guiliang bargained, "Knock off two zeros. Will you sell it for 18 yuan? It's true this book is from the Qianlong era, but the problem is its condition is too poor. The author isn't anyone famous either; it's all about water conservancy techniques. Qing Dynasty water conservancy techniques aren't worth anything now. If its condition were a bit better, I could buy it to add to my collection. How can I collect it when it's been soaked like this?"

The boss, with a cigarette dangling from his lips, said, "18 yuan is too little. I'll give you a discount, 1500 yuan."

Chen Guiliang said, "We're just poor students. What students carry that much cash around to go shopping?"

The words "poor students" were a powerful bargaining tool, implying there wasn't much profit to be squeezed out of them.

The boss showed great mercy, "Alright, seeing as you're students. Take it for 100 yuan."

Chen Guiliang pulled out two 10-yuan bills. "I'll buy it for 20 yuan."

"80 yuan, and I'll throw in two Republican ones for you," the boss said, bundling them in a buy-one-get-two-free deal.

Chen Guiliang didn't want to waste any more time either. He bought the three tattered books for 80 yuan.

Both sides felt they had gotten a good deal.

Once they were far from the stall, Tao Xue asked excitedly, "Did we find a treasure?"

Chen Guiliang said, "It's not clear yet. It might have some academic research value, but it's definitely not worth much money. I plan to donate it to Peking University and see if they find it useful."

"Let me see." Bian Guanyue was also a little curious.

Chen Guiliang took out his phone and made a call, "Hello, Professor Han... This is Chen Guiliang... I'm not calling to ask a question. I just found a book called 'A Record of Things Seen and Heard on River Defense' at a stall. It was written by a Tongzhi in charge of river affairs in the Qing Dynasty. He's named; this Tongzhi is called Zhuang Maode. If you're interested, I'll donate it to Peking University."

Professor Han was a female professor in her fifties who specialized in Chinese historical geography, with a particular expertise in China's historical agricultural geography, social geography, and environmental change.

Even over the phone, Professor Han didn't miss a chance to impart knowledge, "In the Qing Dynasty, the Tongzhi in charge of river affairs was divided into two levels, prefectural and sub-prefectural. Depending on the situation, the highest was a senior fifth-rank official, the lowest a junior sixth-rank. Since your book has a name, it does have a certain research value. What's written inside?"

Chen Guiliang took the book from Bian Guanyue's hands, opened it, and read the legible parts.

After he read a few pages, Professor Han got a little excited.

Professor Han said, "The author of this book is very detailed in his descriptions when explaining the techniques. Generally, ancient books on water conservancy would only briefly state 'remove silt after the flood season.' But you just read 'three days after the summer flood season, when the water is clear and blue, take the silt from the river's center.' Other books basically don't record detailed ratios, but yours says 'for one part silt, a ratio of three parts sand to seven parts mud is best, mix in twenty jin of chopped wheat straw.'"

Chen Guiliang surmised, "This is a handwritten copy, not publicly printed. He probably wrote it in detail to pass down to his descendants. It was a well-kept secret of a Qing Dynasty technocratic family."

Professor Han said, "So it has very high academic research value. It can help restore some of the water conservancy techniques of the Qing Dynasty."

"Since it has research value, I'll bring it to the university to donate it next Monday," Chen Guiliang said.

Professor Han was especially happy, "That's wonderful! I thank you on behalf of the university and the department."

The content of this book was enough for Professor Han to write several papers.

But the book really wasn't worth any money. No one would collect this kind of thing.

After Chen Guiliang hung up the phone, Tao Xue cheered, "Wow, we really found a treasure!"

Chen Guiliang teased her to make her happy, "It's a good thing you dragged me to browse the stalls, or else I would have never come across this book."

"See, I told you we'd find something," Tao Xue said smugly.

Bian Guanyue wasn't looking at the two of them, but walked straight ahead.

The three of them slowly made their way to the teahouse.

The show hadn't started yet, but a lot of people had already arrived.

Chen Guiliang even saw Zhang Guoli, who was paying for a funeral wreath... ahem, a flower basket for Guo Degang.

The reason Guo Degang had become so popular last year was due not only to the efforts of newspaper reporters, but also to the promotion from celebrities like Zhang Guoli and Yuan Li.

At this moment, both Zhang Guoli and his wife, Deng Jie, were there.

"Should we send a flower basket?" Bian Guanyue asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "Let's. Consider it an invitation fee to ask these crosstalk performers to register on Hainei."

Chen Guiliang got up and went to the backstage entrance to register the flower basket information with the stage crew.

A staff member asked, "Which flower basket would you like to send? We have pairs for 80, and also 120 and 200. We also have a super-large flower basket that takes four people to carry, a pair costs 800 yuan."

Chen Guiliang said, "I'll send two pairs of the super-large flower baskets. One pair for Old Guo, and one pair for Yu Qian'er."

The staff member was overjoyed, "May I ask your esteemed name, sir?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Chen Guiliang."

As the staff member registered the name, he wondered why it sounded so familiar.

When Chen Guiliang went to pay, he realized he didn't seem to have enough cash on him, so he asked, "Can I use a card?"

"Huh?"

The staff member was stunned, "We only accept cash here, we don't have a card machine... Please wait a moment."

The staff member rushed backstage and said to Guo Degang, "Master, there's a young man who wants to send two pairs of the 800-yuan flower baskets. One pair for you, and one for Teacher Yu."

Yu Qian'er was playing with his folding fan. Hearing this, he smiled, "Whoa, I even get a share this time."

Guo Degang said happily, "A big boss. Two pairs of large flower baskets, we'll have to do an encore today."

The staff member explained, "But he didn't have enough cash when he went to pay, and he asked if he could use a card."

Guo Degang and Yu Qian'er looked at each other. They had never encountered such a situation.

Yu Qian'er said, "You should get a POS machine here."

Guo Degang thought for a moment and said, "It's not convenient for us to show our faces before the performance. Go invite that big boss in. I'll apologize to him in person; our service is indeed not up to par."

The staff member left immediately and quickly ran back. "The man is gone."

Yu Qian'er said, "Oh my, the big boss couldn't wait. A shame about my big flower basket; it's so rare I get a share."

What was Chen Guiliang doing?

He was looking for Zhang Guoli to borrow money, and to get to know him at the same time.

People in business always have a use for celebrities. Who knows, he might even have to invest in and produce his own movies and TV shows when he starts a video website in the future.

"Teacher Zhang, hello." Chen Guiliang walked over to shake his hand like they were old friends.

Seeing how young he was, Zhang Guoli thought he was a junior from some family.
